units: Agent package initializer imports/exports BaselineAgent and RECAAgent.
BaselineAgent stores numeric parameters and supports epsilon-greedy action selection and reward-driven scalar adaptation.
Baseline state includes parameters plus learning-rate/discount/exploration-style configuration needed for its simple update behavior.
Action choice uses epsilon-greedy behavior over the implemented parameter/value representation.
Reward updates adjust a scalar value/parameter rather than changing the structure of the adaptation mechanism.
Adapt method loops the simple reward update and exposes baseline adaptation behavior for comparison.
RECAAgent stores model_parameters, consequence_memory and structural-modification state in addition to ordinary action/adaptation behavior.
receive_consequence stores the latest consequence and appends it to consequence memory.
Agent generates candidate mutations by perturbing numeric model-parameter values.
evaluate_modification scores a candidate using a placeholder future-viability calculation derived from the candidate/current parameter values.
A candidate modification is accepted when its implemented score is positive; accepted parameters replace the current parameter state.
Accepted structural/parameter states can be retained in the agent's implemented memory/state for later behavior.
Implemented D_c proxy returns the fixed value 1.0.
Implemented C_e proxy is consequence-memory length divided by max(1, number of model parameters).
Implemented A_c proxy is the count of model-parameter keys.
Implemented GV proxy is the product D_c*C_e*A_c.
The code does not attach an explicit semantic type distinguishing a parameter mutation from a deeper mechanism-level structural innovation.
The implemented future-viability score is a local parameter heuristic and does not itself define a future environment horizon or perturbation distribution.
Environment package initializer exposes BaseEnvironment and GridWorld.
BaseEnvironment defines state plus reset/step-style environment interface for benchmark environments.
Base reset semantics reinitialize environment state.
Base step semantics define the environment interaction hook to be specialized by concrete environments.
GridWorld implements a finite grid with position, goal, obstacles and stochastic transition noise.
GridWorld.reset resets position/state for a new episode/trajectory.
GridWorld.step applies an action/noise transition, updates state and returns a numeric reward.
Reward reflects progress/goal/obstacle-style grid behavior encoded by the environment implementation.
Environment includes configurable transition noise so identical nominal actions need not have identical realized transitions.
Defines AgentComparisonResult for storing comparison outputs between RECA and baseline conditions.
compare_agents executes a toy RECA-versus-baseline comparison over changing target/task values and aggregates condition-level outcomes.
Comparison instantiates and updates the simple BaselineAgent condition.
Comparison instantiates RECAAgent and invokes its consequence/adaptation/modification behavior.
Comparison returns in-memory summary structures; this file itself does not contain persisted run results.
The toy comparison does not by itself encode the full multi-seed perturbation/ablation/long-horizon inferential protocol described in benchmark documentation.
Perturbation helper wraps environment interaction and applies a supplied perturbation callback at a selected step.
Helper records pre/post/recovery reward trajectories around the perturbation point.
Perturbation semantics are callback-driven rather than tied to one hard-coded perturbation type.
Reward recovery around a perturbation does not by itself identify which internal structural change caused recovery.
LongHorizonTester is intended to evaluate agents over extended interaction with perturbation and viability tracking.
Tester code expects environment state access, perturbation application and viability-evaluation methods.
Tester expects step results exposing next_state, done and reward fields.
Tester accumulates reward/viability/structural-event trajectory information across long horizons.
Tester includes a phase where the environment is perturbed and subsequent adaptation/recovery is evaluated.
The tester delegates viability meaning to the supplied environment; no universal G_V construct is defined inside this file.
